Pushed a second commit folding in a fix found on hardware before this merged: libgpiod v2 changed `gpioset` to hold the line request open until killed, so the oneshot unit's ExecStart never returned and the unit sat in `activating` forever, blocking `sonic.target` (Type=oneshot has no start timeout by default). The commit switches to the v2 set-and-exit idiom (`--toggle 0`), adds `TimeoutStartSec=30s` as a backstop, and skips cleanly on kernels whose DTB predates the `gpio-line-names` entry. Script/service changes only, no change to the rest of the PR.

Pairs with sonic-net/sonic-linux-kernel#616, which adds the gpio-line-names this service looks up. Safe to merge in either order: on a kernel without the names, the service detects that and skips cleanly, preserving today's behavior.

### Update: current build passes sanity

The latest CI build for this PR passes sanity/smoke on Broadcom XGS hardware
(7260CX3 / Tomahawk-2) -- create_switch comes up clean and forwarding

Perhaps you're aware, and this is technically by design, but keeping this newer 16.1 shim will cause issues if attempting to downgrade to older sonic, like 202505 or 202405. Since the shim sbat level gets written to efi nvram, and is a one-way ratchet, shim 16.1 will require grub sbat version 5. Grub 2.12 is version 5, but grub 2.06 and older are at most version 4. This ratchet will always enforce grub sbat 5 forever if secure boot is enabled, so downgrade is impossible after this. We've run into this when attempting to test other releases on the same testbed, and other vendors/customers may run into issues like this as well.

An alternative to this diff would be to pin shim to an older version on trixie, 15.8, where the sbat level is lower and matches grub of older releases. eg.
```
diff --git a/build_debian.sh b/build_debian.sh
index e91cd08d7..be3fc1b46 100755
--- a/build_debian.sh
+++ b/build_debian.sh
@@ -722,8 +722,18 @@ if [[ $SECURE_UPGRADE_MODE == 'dev' || $SECURE_UPGRADE_MODE == "prod" ]]; then
 	sudo rm $FILESYSTEM_ROOT/grub-efi*.deb

     # debian secure boot dependencies
+    # Add snapshot repo for shim-unsigned 15.8 (not available in current repos)
+    SHIM_SNAPSHOT_LIST=$FILESYSTEM_ROOT/etc/apt/sources.list.d/sonic-shim-snapshot.list
+    echo "deb [check-valid-until=no] https://snapshot.debian.org/archive/debian/20260711T022200Z/ trixie main" | \
+        sudo tee $SHIM_SNAPSHOT_LIST
+    sudo chroot $FILESYSTEM_ROOT apt-get update
+
     sudo LANG=C DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive chroot $FILESYSTEM_ROOT apt-get -y install      \
-        shim-unsigned
+        shim-unsigned=15.8-1
+
+    # Remove snapshot repo
+    sudo rm $SHIM_SNAPSHOT_LIST
+    sudo chroot $FILESYSTEM_ROOT apt-get update

     if [ ! -f $SECURE_UPGRADE_SIGNING_CERT ]; then
         echo "Error: SONiC SECURE_UPGRADE_SIGNING_CERT=$SECURE_UPGRADE_SIGNING_CERT key missing"
```

I'm curious of your thoughts on this, and how letting sonic shim and grub move forward may affect vendors' and customers' test and validation flows.

@spilkey-cisco Yes the newer sonic images with latest shim will block installing older sonic images. This is discussed in Platform WG and @saiarcot895 agreed to add this in the community release notes. 

Keeping the shim and grub pinned to older versions is not a long term solution and will cause sonic to not consume various CVE fixes that went in upstream. We will face the same issues again during forky upgrade next year if we don't make the move now. 

Downgrades can still be down using sonic to sonic install option instead of ONIE. For continued support of this we have an issue - https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/issues/28845

If you have to use onie to downgrade to older sonic then please use the approach to unpack the older shell archive say 202412-sonic.bin image and update the grub and shim to later versions and repack it before installing the older image via ONIE. 

This is not ideal but debian maintainers expected this and still made the decision anyway to block installation of older images.

@tirupatihemanth Thanks for the details, and confirmation! My suggestion was only meant to be temporary until a consensus was made anyway, but it sounds like the decision is already there. Despite the issues that have come up recently, I do agree it is the correct decision from a security viewpoint. Since both grub and shim are unpinned with this PR, ideally we should not run into an SBAT issue like this again. However, maybe it would also be a good idea to pin both (16.1 shim and grub 2.12 today), and only purposefully move the versions forward after test and review.

> If you have to use onie to downgrade to older sonic then please use the approach to unpack the older shell archive say 202412-sonic.bin image and update the grub and shim to later versions and repack it before installing the older image via ONIE.

This should be an update in a workspace, and repack it using the make command to build, right? The entire bin file should be signed to ensure authenticity, though I don't think that is checked yet during image install.

Pinning to a specific version here might be a bit more trouble than it's worth, since we would then need to monitor for new versions that get released and update it manually. Additionally, there is version pinning/constraint infra present today that ensures that each commit of SONiC builds with a specific version of each package.

Regarding the signature verification, if you're using the `sonic-installer install ...` command on a system with secure boot enabled, it should the checking the authenticity of the entire bin file. If you're using any other method (including installing from ONIE), it is not checked.
